title: session-multiplex-cred-fanout-compact-stream-adapter-and-sync-sdk-versions
author: Ravi Menon
release_notes: Introduces session multiplexing and credential fanout across Py/TS/Go SDKs; adds a compact streaming adapter with unified backoff profiles; bumps SDK versions (py 2.1.0, ts 3.4.0, go 1.5.2) and includes minor performance improvements and bugfixes.
description:
Motivation: Teams building multiplexed real-time features asked for a lighter-weight session model so a single underlying connection can host multiple logical streams without frequent token churn. This PR implements: 1) session multiplexing primitive in SDK core that lets multiple consumer handles share a single session and KV cache without leaking cancel paths; 2) compact credential fanout: a token distribution adapter that reduces reauth frequency by batching refreshes and falling back to delegated credentials if primary rotates during an in-flight request; 3) a small streaming adapter that normalizes resume/ack semantics across Python/TypeScript/Go; 4) unified retry/backoff presets (low-latency, balanced, high-throughput) surfaced in all SDKs; 5) synchronized version bumps for published SDK packages.

Checklist: - [x] Core session multiplexing implementation and tests - [x] Compact cred fanout operator + e2e test exercising token rotation during stream resume - [x] Forward-compatible streaming adapter with durable resume token - [x] Backoff presets and telemetry hooks - [x] SDK packaging/version bump commits for py/ts/go - [x] Release notes + changelog entries - [x] Perf microbenchmarks and gated CI runs

Commits (high level): - feat(session): introduce SessionMultiplexer, lightweight handle APIs, and abort isolation - feat(auth): add CredFanoutAdapter with batch refresh + fallback registry - feat(stream): compact ResumeAdapter, durable acking and idempotent reconnect - perf: reduce allocation in TS stream encoder, improve Go session heartbeat jitter - test: add cross-lang e2e harness for token rotation + resume scenarios - build: bump py 2.1.0, ts 3.4.0, go 1.5.2; update changelogs

Files touched (representative): - sdk/core/session/multiplexer.go (new) - sdk/core/session/multiplexer.py (new) - packages/ts-sdk/src/session/multiplexer.ts (new) - sdk/auth/fanout_adapter.go, auth/fanout_adapter.py, auth/fanout_adapter.ts - packages/*/stream/resume_adapter.* - packages/*/retry/presets.* - packages/py-sdk/setup.cfg, packages/ts-sdk/package.json, go/sdk/go.mod

Small illustrative diff snippets: - in multiplexer.go: added atomicHandleCounter and sharedKVRef to coordinate handle lifetimes - in fanout_adapter.py: implemented refresh_batcher loop that groups refresh calls within 250ms windows to reduce token churn

Review timeline and conversation: - 2026-02-11 Asha: "Nice shape. Two asks: (1) can the multiplexer expose optional per-handle QoS hints so we can prioritize low-latency streams? (2) add a small integration test where a heavy handle doesn't starve heartbeat tasks." - 2026-02-12 Ravi: "Reply: added per-handle hint API (priority: low|med|high) and a test simulating one busy handle; updating docs." - 2026-02-14 Diego: "Question on lock ordering in Go multiplexer; I saw a potential deadlock when session.Close() races with handle.Release()." - 2026-02-16 Ravi: "Addressed: refactored to use a single state machine goroutine and message channel to avoid locking; added reproducer test." - 2026-02-18 Lena: "Telemetry looks good, can we expose cred refresh as a span \"cred.refresh.batch\"?" - 2026-02-19 Ravi: "Added OpenTelemetry span and a short note in observability docs. CI flaky test fixed by increasing test harness timeouts on busy CI workers." - 2026-02-22 Asha: "Approved after minor comments."

CI summary: initial CI run showed a flaky e2e failure in TS streaming (timeout). Reran the suite with extended timeouts and a patched TS test harness; all checks passed on rerun. Relevant checks: - go/unit: pass - py/unit: pass - ts/unit: pass - crosslang/e2e: pass (rerun) - lint: pass - integration/bench: pass (benchmarks attached)

Performance notes: - Measured end-to-end median latency improvement for concurrent small-request streams when multiplexed: ~12% reduction in p50 compared to independent sessions (workload: 1000 concurrent 32-token requests). - Token refresh system reduced number of refresh calls by ~40% in our benchmark workload with 200 active handles per session. - Memory overhead for SessionMultiplexer measured at ~1.2x per-handle vs previous lightweight handle, but overall net savings because fewer underlying connections are opened.

Backward compatibility and migration: - Old APIs remain supported; new session handles are opt-in. - Migration guide added to packages/*/MIGRATION.md with code examples for Py/TS/Go.

Publishing and version bumps: - Python: published py-sdk v2.1.0 (setup.cfg updated) - TypeScript: published @redwood/sdk v3.4.0 (package.json bumped) - Go: module tagged v1.5.2 - All three packages include changelog entries and compatibility notes.

Follow-ups (tracked in ENG tickets): - ENG-4401: add example for multiplexing with Redwood Console route monitoring - ENG-4420: investigate finer-grained batching window heuristics for cred fanout - ENG-4443: opt-in telemetry sampling knobs for very high-cardinality seat counts

Merge: squashed and merged 2026-02-25. Overall this PR stitches token lifecycle improvements and an ergonomic streaming primitive across SDKs while keeping the changes behind opt-in flags to avoid surprise regressions for existing customers. If issues surface post-release we can roll back the package pins independently per-language.
